name: AI visibility audit for an online store
summary: A store owner or marketer gets a dated audit of how the store reads to AI assistants and shopping agents, from its own saved public pages: eighteen fixed checks with evidence, a fix list in priority order, and a record of what the assistants actually said. Nothing on the store is changed.

sources.title: Fully Powered AI's AI visibility audit for Shopify stores in its public Shopify repository (MIT): the eighteen checks and what each reads, the priority table and its thresholds, the feed and open-web routes, the answer-check sheet with its connection rule, and the rules that a missing page is never a failure and nothing on the store is changed.

sources.contribution: The stance that the work makes a site readable and accurate rather than steering a recommendation; presenting a crawler block as the owner's choice; asking an assistant the customers' own questions and recording exactly what came back, with no score, repeated monthly.
Counting questions that name the brand apart from those that do not, and counting cited sources apart from mentions, when recording what answer engines say.

Fixed checks over saved page facts so that two runs compare, with image alt coverage and organization profile links among the signals; here each check keeps its own outcome and no combined score is made.
Stating in every report what was measured directly and what was only inferred, and never making up a measurement.
Reading the robots file by user-agent group, checking the sitemap and the structured data, and giving each finding a fix and a priority.
Checking the discovery files an assistant reads (robots, sitemap, llms.txt and llms-full.txt) and that the facts are in the HTML the server sends.

Storefront audit areas, among them structured data and product pages, narrowed here to what an assistant reads: the product and organization structured data and the title, description and heading checks, with no conversion or app-stack advice.
